summary.headline: Angel One Q2 FY27: consolidated PAT up 58.2% YoY to ₹3.35 bn on revenue of ₹14.3 bn (+18.9%); standalone OPM 48.9%.
summary.overview: Revenue held broadly flat sequentially despite softer trading after regulatory changes, while profit grew much faster on operating leverage and a larger client funding book. Consolidated operating margin rose to 45.1% from 34.5% a year ago; normalised for IPL spend and ESOP reversals it was 43.8% versus 43.6% in Q1. Management kept the standalone broking-plus-distribution margin guidance at about 45% annually and reported record average funding book (₹74.5 bn) and record credit distribution in September (annualised run rate ₹33 bn). Client additions were about 1.5 mn, up 11.6% QoQ. Management said October F&O industry ADTO was up about 39% month-to-date versus September (as of 14 October) and linked near-term upside to the SEBI closing auction session (CAS) circular.

financial_highlights.change: +58% YoY (58.2% as stated in opening remarks)
vs 34.5% a year ago (>1,000 bps); 43.8% normalised vs 43.6% QoQ

segments.name: Broking (direct/assisted)
segments.commentary: Gross broking share fell to ~55% of revenue from ~60% a year ago. Net broking income split is ~75% direct and ~25% AP channel. September average daily orders rebounded to 5.8 mn, up ~12% from August.

segments.name: Market share
segments.commentary: Retail F&O turnover share 22.1% for the quarter, rising to 22.5% in September; cash share moderated. Options premium turnover share 19.7%. Commodities turnover more than doubled YoY with share down to 44% as the market expanded.

segments.name: Lending (MTF/funding)
segments.commentary: Interest income ₹5.1 bn. About 84% of funded clients have exposure below ₹100,000; 82% of closing book is under 30 days old. Lending rate held at 14.99% despite higher RBI-linked borrowing costs. Management said delinquencies remain negligible.

segments.name: Distribution
segments.commentary: Distribution income ~₹71 crore in the quarter, about 5% of revenue, helped by credit distribution and IPO activity. Management does not disclose the split. Regular plans are about one-third of MF distribution.

segments.name: Wealth (Ionic Wealth)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹160 bn, up 19.1% QoQ. Management said margins will be in line with industry (ultra-HNI industry yields near 0.5%) and that the book is focused on annuity-based assets. Some AUM is in custody and does not earn fees; management called this a very small number.

segments.name: Asset Management
segments.commentary: AUM about ₹6 bn. Management is evaluating a comprehensive play and plans to bring in a new leader; no timeline given.

segments.name: New businesses (drag)
segments.commentary: Cash burn from new businesses at about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, up from 2.5%-3% about six quarters ago.

guidance_outlook: Standalone broking-plus-distribution operating margin guided at about 45% on an annual basis; quarterly variation expected. Management said 40-45% is comfortable and it may go towards 50% at times.
Consolidated operating margin guided at 40-45% in the near term; management expects improvement as other businesses contribute meaningfully over the next 2-3 years.
Employee cost guided at about ₹1,100 crore for FY27 including ESOP cost, flat YoY; employee count about 3,050 as of 30 September with backfills slowed.
Brand (IPL) spend expected to decline as a percentage of revenue over time.
Lending rate unchanged at 14.99%. Dividend payout continues quarterly, subject to capital needs.
capex_capacity: Credit distribution hit a record in September, with annualised run rate of ₹33 bn; management expects new highs over the next few quarters.
Early beta of loan against securities (LAS) launched; to be scaled with discipline.
Upgraded probability of default model used for credit distribution.
US stocks piloted via IFSC GAP licence (GIFT City) with a US brokerage partner; live pilot with a set of customers and orders flowing.
Cybersecurity stack strengthened with AI-driven vulnerability detection and automated remediation.
demand_pricing: Management cited the SEBI closing auction session (CAS) circular issued 20 October as a tailwind; October F&O industry ADTO up about 39% month-to-date vs September (options, to 14 October).
Client additions of about 1.5 mn in Q2, up 11.6% QoQ; management says activation trends have improved and NSE active share rose each month of the quarter.
SIP registrations up nearly 12% QoQ; management declined to read much into the September decline.
Management sees F&O pricing as right and is not planning to change it; price elasticity exists but trust is a key driver.
Net broking realisation rose partly on commodities mix; per-segment realisations not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 45% margin guidance include IPL spend and how is employee cost so low?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the ~45% annual guidance for broking plus distribution includes all expenses including IPL. Employee cost fell due to attrition and one-time costs in Q1; FY27 employee cost guided at ~₹1,100 crore, flat YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross client acquisition slower than the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said acquisitions were up 11% vs Q1 and the company is focused on activation and marginal CAC across channels, including AP, performance marketing and organic. Management said it would invest where growth is available at the right price.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP registrations drop in September?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said SIP registration numbers vary month-to-month and can be optical (counting edits); a broader period gives a better read, and management tracks SIP inflows and active SIPs.

qa_highlights.question: How is rising borrowing cost affecting MTF and competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said lending rate stays at 14.99% with no change planned; borrowing cost rose marginally after the RBI benchmark hike but is within tolerance, with NIMs not materially affected. Bhavin said blue-chip and good stocks make up over 85% of the MTF book.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wealth AUM fee yield and how much is earning fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Shobhit said margins will track industry levels (about 0.5% in ultra-HNI) and most of the book is annuity-based. Amit said assets were acquired through the year, so applying yield to closing AUM overstates revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the drag from new businesses on EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Vineet said the cash burn from new businesses is about 3.5%-4% of EBITDA margin, versus about 2.5%-3% six quarters ago when scale was low.

qa_highlights.question: Will the closing auction session circular help F&O volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Ambarish said the circular provides clarity and is a tailwind for near-term F&O, and that pricing is working and not under review.

risks_watch: Regulatory changes (F&O and CAS) are reducing market volumes; management expects a gradual recovery but timing is uncertain.
Cash segment share fell while MTF grew; management attributes this to segment mix, but it is worth tracking.
Competition from new corporate-backed brokerages with lower pricing; management says trust and brand support pricing.
Net active clients have fallen over two years even as total users rose (questioned by Mohit Surana); activation trend is the key metric to watch.
IPL and brand spend, plus AP channel and new business cash burn of 3.5%-4%, weigh on margins.
Insurance commission reset (IRDAI consultation) and US stock pilot are early-stage and not yet material.
summary.management_tone: Confident on profitability, margins and the CAS-driven October recovery, while cautious on the timing of volume recovery. Management was evasive on product per customer, LTV, and new-business margins, and declined to give specific FY28 margin targets.
key_quotes: Despite the regulatory environment, our consolidated revenue and PAT grew 18.9% and 58.2% year-over-year, respectively.
Importantly, after normalizing for seasonal IPL expenditure and ESOP-related reversals, consolidated operating margins remained stable at 43.8% compared to 43.6% in the preceding quarter.
On a consol basis, so the guidance is anywhere between 40% to 45% in the near term.

growth.why: Management held standalone broking-plus-distribution margin guidance at about 45% annually and guided consolidated OPM at 40-45% near term, with no revenue growth guidance; growth backing rests on record funding book (₹74.5 bn average, +40.5% YoY), record credit distribution (₹33 bn annualised run rate), and client additions of ~1.5 mn, with no specific new capacity or orders quantified.
